title: Switching corollary: restrictions with no narrow CNF
statement:
Let $f$ be a DNF formula on $n \ge 1$ variables in which no variable occurs more than once within any single term, and let $w, s \in \bbn$ satisfy $5s \le n$ and $\mathrm{width}(f) \le w$ (that is, every term of $f$ has at most $w$ literals). For a restriction $\rho$ that fixes some variables and leaves the others free, write $f\!\restriction_\rho$ for the Boolean function obtained by evaluating $f$ with the fixed coordinates set by $\rho$ and the free coordinates supplied as input. Then the number of restrictions $\rho$ leaving exactly $s$ of the $n$ variables free for which $f\!\restriction_\rho$ agrees with no CNF formula of width at most $w$ satisfies
\[
  \bigl|\{\rho : \rho \text{ leaves exactly } s \text{ variables free, and } f\!\restriction_\rho \text{ has no width-}{\le}w\text{ CNF}\}\bigr| \cdot n^{w}
  \;\le\; \binom{n}{s}\, 2^{\,n-s}\,(10sw)^{w}.
\]
hypotheses_covered: f is a DNF formula on n variables
no variable repeats within any term (distinct literals with equal variable are identical, and terms have no duplicate literals)
no CNF of width ≤ w equals the restricted function f↾ρ pointwise
replaced:
Under the same hypotheses as Theorem~\ref{thm:switching_lemma},
\[
  \bigl|\{\rho : \mathrm{IsRestriction}\ s\ \rho,\ f|_\rho
    \text{ has no CNF of width}\le w\}\bigr| \cdot n^w
  \le \mathrm{numSRestrictions}(n,s)\,(10sw)^w.
\]
